nodes.label: The most active constraint is the coupling itself
nodes.rationale: The bound that cuts the most is not a hydrogenic or Pauli cap shaping a single subshell but the one bound tying the two ends of the transition together, so most active and is the coupling are the same fact about the same bound.

nodes.label: g <= q, the sole target-to-source bound
nodes.rationale: g <= q reads placed <= removed: electrons arriving at the target cannot outnumber those the source gave up. It is the only bound in the whole definition relating a target coordinate to a source coordinate, read from the constraint graph.

nodes.label: Seven constraints ranked by marginal exclusion over the Lambda-8 box
nodes.rationale: The measure is marginal by design — a constraint's activity is the exclusion no other constraint would make in its absence, counted over cells clearing every other bound: g<=q 673, q<=k 575, k<=4l+2 564, l<=n-1 308, 2S<=k 300, f<=e-1 200, k>=1 25, g<=4f+2 24.

nodes.label: Lambda is a cylinder over the transfer, not a rectangle of states
nodes.rationale: Remove g <= q and the two ends of the tree fall apart into an index of source configurations beside an index of target configurations — a product of states; keep it and each cell is a move conserving what it transfers.
